correctness.rationale: For m,n>=3 all pairs have a common neighbor and all mixed >=3-faces have a unique common-neighbor center. The intersection of each center simplex with the row/column-boundary complete-edge core is homotopy equivalent to a graph with (m-1)(n-1) parallel edges, hence its contractible simplex contributes precisely (m-1)(n-1)-1 relative two-spheres. Intersections of center simplices away from the core are empty. Relative homology vanishes above degree two. Row/column boundary chains then calculate integral high homology, and their alternating orientations verify every group-action sign. A standalone exhaustive checker corroborates finite cases, without being used as universal proof.

value.rationale: This natural two-parameter graph family is central in line graphs, product graphs, and equivariant topological combinatorics. An exact graph-size-independent cofiber calculation explains why mixed high-dimensional faces contribute only 2-dimensional topology, while all degree>=3 integral homology is torsion-free and explicitly carries permutation/sign representations. The theorem differentiates open and closed neighborhood constructions even on the same graph and is not implied by a census or a one-parameter specialization.
